title: The maze: a hand on the wall
reflection: Your program got Byte out of mazes it had never seen. Why does keeping a hand on the wall always work? When wouldn't it?

steps.goal: MINE has built a winding corridor in front of Byte, different every time, with a gold block at its end. Bring Byte right in front of the gold, walking only along the corridor.
steps.not_yet: Not yet: Byte has to stop right in front of the gold, without climbing or breaking the walls.
hints: MINE has put a gold block in the highlighted slot: byte.compare() is true when the block in front is gold. while not byte.compare() do ... end repeats until Byte faces it.
Inside the loop: if not byte.detect() then go forward; else turn right, and if there's a wall there too (and it isn't the gold), turn left twice.
block_hints: MINE has put a gold block in the highlighted slot: "block in front same as the slot's?" is true when Byte faces the gold. Use "repeat until" with it.
Inside: an "if" with "not block in front?": "move forward"; else "turn right", and if "block in front?" and not the gold, "turn left" twice.

steps.goal: Now it's a real maze, with dead ends, and a new one every time. Get Byte out: right in front of the gold, without climbing or digging.
steps.not_yet: Not yet: Byte has to stop right in front of the gold, walking only along the corridors.
hints: Keep your right hand on the wall and you'll get out of any maze like this one: at every step, turn right; while there's a wall in front (that isn't the gold), turn left; then one step forward.
while not byte.compare() do: byte.turnRight(), then while byte.detect() and not byte.compare() do byte.turnLeft() end, then if not byte.compare() then byte.forward() end.
block_hints: Keep your right hand on the wall and you'll get out of any maze like this one: at every step, turn right; while there's a wall in front (that isn't the gold), turn left; then one step forward.
"repeat until" the gold: "turn right"; "repeat while" "block in front?" and not the gold: "turn left"; if not the gold: "move forward".

steps.goal: Get Byte out of a new maze again, and at the gold make it say how many steps it took. Count them with a variable: MINE counts them too.
steps.not_yet: Not yet: Byte has to stop in front of the gold and say how many steps it took.
hints: Before the loop, local steps = 0. Each time Byte goes forward, steps = steps + 1.
At the end: mine.say("I took " .. steps .. " steps"). The .. joins texts and numbers.
block_hints: In Variables, make a variable "steps". Before the loop, "set steps to 0"; after "move forward", "change steps by 1".
At the end, "say" with "create text with": "I took ", steps, " steps".
